FramePresignRequest.description:
Declare a raw LiDAR frame upload targeting the sensor-log layout.

Unlike the generic uploader (flat ``uploads/``), a frame lands under
``raw/<sensor_id>/<date>/`` so it becomes selectable as a sensor log in the
create-run form and feeds the detection pipeline.
FramePresignRequest.title: FramePresignRequest

PresignUploadRequest.description: What the browser declares before uploading directly to B2.
PresignUploadRequest.title: PresignUploadRequest

PresignUploadResponse.description:
A short-lived presigned PUT the browser uploads to, plus the exact
headers it must send. `Content-Length` and `content-type` are signed into
the URL, so B2 rejects a body of any other size or type.
PresignUploadResponse.title: PresignUploadResponse

info.description: Local API for MMDetection3D LiDAR Dataset: ingest raw LiDAR point-cloud frames to Backblaze B2, run MMDetection3D locally to produce per-frame 3D detection/segmentation annotations, archive checkpoints, and tie every frame to a dataset manifest — all over the S3-compatible API. This contract documents the sample's local API, not a hosted public endpoint.
info.title: MMDetection3D LiDAR Dataset API

re-run extraction, so it is billed at the tighter 'write' rate-limit tier
(see runtime/ratelimit.py) to bound egress/cost amplification.

post.description:
Presign a direct-to-B2 PUT for a raw LiDAR frame in the sensor-log layout.

Writes under ``raw/<sensor_id>/<date>/`` so the frame feeds the detection
flow and the sensor log becomes selectable in the create-run form — unlike
the generic uploader's flat ``uploads/`` prefix.
Confirm a LiDAR frame just uploaded directly to B2 is valid.

post.description:
Validate a declared upload and hand back a presigned PUT.

The browser uploads the bytes straight to B2 with the returned URL, so they
never traverse this Function — that is what lifts Vercel's ~4.5 MB payload
ceiling. Size and content-type are signed into the URL (see the service).
Confirm an object just uploaded directly to B2 is valid and visible.
